action: Gatwick advises drop-off zone users to use one of the alternative payment methods listed on the London Gatwick website.
date_note: Cedar News (24 November) reports the airport's email to drivers as sent on Tuesday 24 November; the page gives no earlier day for the unauthorised access.
exec: Gatwick says personal details and, in some very limited cases, partial card payment information of AutoPay drop-off users may have been accessed through a third-party system.
geo_basis: Gatwick Airport, West Sussex, UK; airport location, not the location of the third-party system
impact: According to Cedar News's account of the airport's email, names, contact details, AutoPay login information and vehicle registrations may have been exposed, and in some cases card brand, last four digits and expiry date.
plain: Gatwick Airport says it switched off its AutoPay drop-off payment service after unauthorised access to a third-party system. A spokesperson says personal details, and in some very limited cases partial card details, may have been accessed.
summary: Gatwick Airport disabled its AutoPay drop-off payment system as a precaution after a report of unauthorised access to AutoPay, a third-party system. A Gatwick spokesperson, quoted by the Mirror, said the data that may have been accessed includes AutoPay login information, contact and personal details, vehicle and drop-off information and, in some very limited cases, partial card payment information. The investigation is ongoing; no count of people is given.
title: Gatwick Airport disables AutoPay after unauthorised access to a third-party system, warns of possible data exposure

validation.note: Cedar News and the Mirror (via AOL) are independent publishers; the Mirror quotes a Gatwick spokesperson. BBC and Mirror pages could not be loaded; AOL copy of the Mirror read. GB News 402, London Now carries no date.
